embeds.title: 🔴 Windows BitLocker Zero-Day Gives Access to Protected Drives; PoC Released
embeds.description:
A cybersecurity researcher known as Chaotic Eclipse or Nightmare Eclipse has publicly disclosed proof-of-concept exploits for two unpatched Microsoft Windows vulnerabilities: YellowKey (a BitLocker bypass affecting Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025) and GreenPlasma (a privilege escalation flaw). The researcher claims YellowKey functions as a BitLocker backdoor by exploiting NTFS transactions in the Windows Recovery Environment, allowing access to BitLocker-protected drives without credentials on TPM-only configurations. GreenPlasma is claimed to enable arbitrary memory-section creation for privilege escalation to SYSTEM permissions. The researcher stated the disclosures were driven by dissatisfaction with Microsoft's handling of previous vulnerability reports (BlueHammer/CVE-2026-33825 and RedSun).
**Sources:** BleepingComputer • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-33825 • **Access:** USB drive with specially crafted FsTx files or EFI partition modification
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
